member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.DevicePreference
member.summary: Which device the user meant. Accepts vid:pid hex (the precise, portable key — 346e:0006 is a MOZA R12), #N for an index, or a case-insensitive name substring. Also knows which "controllers" are virtual pads that must never be picked as a wheel.
member.remarks: vJoy reports 8 axes / 128 buttons like a MOZA R12, advertises force feedback, and often enumerates first; a game or mod that takes "first FFB device" picks it and every force is absorbed silently. That cost a long debugging session and a wrongly-filed upstream bug (OutRun2006Tweaks-FFB, commit 02e3028). Blocklist first, rank FFB-capable real devices, then apply the preference.

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.ForceModel
member.summary: Composable force model over : the structure that carried over between four games, with the constants that did not left as settings. Output is normalised -1..1 before .

remarks.para: Sign convention: positive output pushes the wheel toward positive steer (the direction the car is turning) — i.e. it is anti-centring — and the model produces negative output for a positive steer input, which is centring. Which DirectInput sign that maps to is a per-wheel fact handled by ; measure it.

The watches the inputs, because the source signal decides more than the model: art of rally's aligning torque reversed past the slip peak, and OutRun's steer input sat at zero through corners while the model's spring term silently produced nothing.

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.ForceShaper
member.summary: The output conditioning chain every wheel mod ends up writing: deadzone, dual-rate smoothing, soft saturation, slew limiting with event bypass, low-speed fade, warm-up ramp, gain and inversion. Pure math, no device.
member.remarks: Order matters and is fixed (see knowledge/FFB-SIGNAL-DESIGN.md): deadzone → EMA → soft saturation → slew → fade → ramp → gain/invert → clamp. Structural force goes through all of it; an isEvent update (crash impulse, shift pulse) bypasses the EMA and slew so it arrives as a pulse rather than a shove. Rules lifted from OutRun2006Tweaks-FFB (chain), art-of-sim-rally (fade, Strength as the only dial) and cruisn-collection (slew and clamp as the instability ladder).

member.name: T:Dbce.Wheel.Ffb.WheelFfbNative
member.summary: Managed binding to WheelFfb.dll, the toolkit's native DirectInput force-feedback and device layer.

remarks.para: The DLL is loaded by absolute path before any DllImport resolves: Unity Mod Manager mods and BepInEx plugins live in folders that are not on the loader's search path. On Mono a LoadLibraryW preload is enough (a later import by base name finds the loaded module); on CoreCLR a NativeLibrary.SetDllImportResolver is installed through reflection when the API exists, so the same assembly serves both runtimes.
Every call is guarded: a missing DLL or export records and leaves the game running without force feedback rather than throwing inside a physics step.
